Subject: Paperwork callouts & order-form synthesis for 2027 renewal

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are two items from our side to accelerate the renewal: an annotated MSA with my in-line callouts (Redwood_MSA_annotated.pdf) and a proposed merged order form (OrderForm_v3.docx) that folds the capacity uplift and billing schedule you asked for.

Key callouts:
- Term: we draft a 12-month renewal term with one automatic renewal; legal flagged the cancellation notice window (30 days) — see MSA §3.2.
- Capacity: order form currently lists +35% token uplift for Q1–Q2 2027; we marked a tiered ramp tied to usage (lines 18–26).
- Billing: we proposed monthly invoicing net-30; if procurement needs net-45 we can add a 1.5% early-pay credit to bridge negotiating points.
- SLA credits: Legal wants to cap credits at 20% of monthly invoice; customer success is asking for 30% floor on sustained outages.

Ask: can you review the attached and send any explicit redlines or a short summary of must-haves by EOD Tuesday (Nov 24)? If you prefer, we can hop on a 20–30 minute call Tuesday morning to go line-by-line.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_annotated.pdf (annotated), OrderForm_v3.docx (proposed merge, draft)

Thanks —

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the annotated MSA. We kicked this to procurement and legal and they returned a few high-level positions:

1) Payment terms: procurement is pushing for net-45. They said their internal cadence requires 45 days but are open to a 1–1.5% early-pay incentive.
2) Auto-renew term: they prefer a 6-month auto-renew window (we're trying to avoid being locked in for long) — we noted your proposed 12 months.
3) SLA credits: we asked if Redwood can add a 72-hour escalation SLA (phone escalation to an on-call engineering lead) before crediting.

I've attached our markups (Hawthorne_Responses_2027.docx) with inline notes. Most of the order-form capacity numbers look fine; procurement just wants the invoice cadence clarified (which lines up with the payment-term ask).

We can do a call Tuesday 10am PT if that works.

Subject: Fwd: Hawthorne markups — legal comments and suggested language

Ben / Monica —

Forwarding Sophie’s note with a quick legal read. I pulled the change-levels into one document (OrderForm_merged_v4.docx) and annotated the firm positions below. Please review and confirm whether these are deal-breakers or negotiable tradeoffs before we call procurement.

Laura's legal summary (high level):
- Term and Auto-Renew: Legal prefers 12 months; commercial may accept 6 months if we tighten the non-renewal notice to 45 days instead of 30. Proposed compromise: 12-month initial term + opt-in 6-month renewals thereafter for customer with 45-day notice window. (See redlines, OrderForm_merged_v4.docx lines 12–20).
- Payment terms: We should avoid net-45 by default. Offer: net-30 standard, net-45 acceptable with a 1.25% administrative fee or an early-pay discount of 1.25% for net-30.
- SLA & Escalation: We can commit to a 72-hour response for Level 1 escalations and provide an on-call engineering contact within that window; however, credit-execution remains capped at 20% monthly invoice. Recommend we keep credit cap and add the escalation SLA as a non-credit remedy.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ben to propose the compromise (12-month initial, opt-in 6-month renewals, 45-day notice) and the payment trade (net-30 or net-45 + 1.25% / early-pay 1.25% discount).
2) Monica to prepare the final merged order-form for signature after Sophie confirms procurement’s stance.
3) If procurement insists on net-45 with no fee, escalate to RevOps for finance sign-off.

I’ve attached OrderForm_merged_v4.docx with tracked language.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & Contract Ops (acting legal liaison)
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: OrderForm_merged_v4.docx (merged + legal annotations)

Subject: RE: Paperwork callouts & order-form synthesis for 2027 renewal — proposed path to signature

Sophie —

Thanks for the markups and for looping procurement in. To keep momentum, here’s the path I’m proposing (based on Laura’s notes):

Accepted / agreed in principle:
- Capacity uplift and ramp — accepted as drafted in OrderForm_merged_v4.docx (we kept a tiered ramp to avoid early over-commit).
- 72-hour escalation: Redwood will add a named on-call escalation contact and agree to a 72-hour initial response window; escalation will be recorded in the incident log.

Open / conditional items:
- Term: Redwood proposes an initial 12-month term with the option for customer to elect 6-month renewals thereafter (opt-in). If Hawthorne prefers 6-month auto-renew math for flexibility, we’d like a 45-day notice window. Please confirm preferred path.
- Payment terms: Redwood’s standard is net-30. We can accept net-45 if Hawthorne takes a 1.25% administrative fee (or we can offer 1.25% early-pay discount for net-30). Which would procurement prefer?
- SLA credits cap: legal holds at 20% monthly invoice. If credit cap is unacceptable, flag it now so we can escalate.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sophie to confirm payment preference (net-30 with early-pay 1.25% or net-45 with 1.25% admin fee) and term preference (12m initial vs 6m auto-renew).
2) On confirmation, Monica will publish the final OrderForm_merged_v4.docx and I’ll send the DocuSign envelope for signature (targeting Nov 24 send).

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC123 (will contain merged order form + signature flow)

If it helps, we can take the 20–30 minute sync Tuesday 10am PT — I’ll stand by to make any live edits.

Best,
